title: Jest · był · będzie zamknięty
note:
B2-SPINE Block 7 unit 3, spine O5 — the last unit of Block 7 and the CONSTRUCTION half of a load split stated one node earlier. b2_participle_pass was the FORM and its agreement, and every sentence in it was X jest <participle> in the present; this unit moves that sentence through time (byl / bedzie) and gives the construction its name. The previous pack's final slide told the learner exactly this edge was coming, so the two are read as a pair rather than as an overlap.

ZERO NEW LEMMAS, and the arithmetic is honest rather than a boast: every participle comes from the unit before, and byl / byla / bylo (past_byc, A2) and bedzie (bedzie + copular_future) have been owned for a hundred nodes. teaches_lemmas is legitimately empty on the adj_gen / copular_future / adj_inst / ze_clauses / indirect_q convention — the pack teaches a STRUCTURE, not words. What is new is that two owned pieces are allowed to combine, and that the combination has a name.

THE REAL CONTENT IS DOUBLE AGREEMENT, and it is the one thing in the unit that can actually be got wrong. In the past BOTH words carry the gender and they must carry the same one: Sklep byl zamkniety / Apteka byla zamknieta / Biuro bylo zamkniete. Slide 2 puts the three rows under each other so the two columns of endings line up on the page. The predictable error is changing the tense and leaving the participle behind, and the pack says so in terms.

THE FUTURE IS THE ASYMMETRY AND IT PAYS BACK A2's GIFT. a2_bedzie's headline was that the future of byc has NO gender — one word for a man, a woman and a table. That is still true, and the participle after it still agrees anyway, so the future is the odd one out: Sklep bedzie zamkniety / Apteka bedzie zamknieta. In the past both words move; in the future only the second one does. This is the unit's second fact and it costs nothing, because both halves are already owned — only their interaction is new. Slide 4 then closes the loop from the other side: with a masculine noun fixed (obiad), the participle never moves and ONLY the copula carries the time.

THE PASSIVE IS NAMED, per AGENTS' register ruling — the learner is linguistically inclined and Polish is a case language he is here for. Slide 1 names it, says what it does (the subject is what the work was done TO, not who did it), and points out that English builds it the same way, with a form of 'to be' plus a participle, so the machinery is new in neither language. No cute framing, no 'free gift'.

STATE PASSIVE ONLY, AND THE PACK SAYS SO RATHER THAN LETTING IT PASS AS THE WHOLE STORY. Sklep byl zamkniety describes how things STOOD, the result; the dynamic passive naming the moment of closing needs zostac, which is verified NEW (along with zostal and zostanie) and is fenced to C1 by O5. Slide 5 states that a second passive exists and that its verb is not taught here — an accepted gap named out loud, on the b2_powinien precedent of naming the missing past of moc rather than letting the learner discover it by failing.

THE AGENT PHRASE IS IMPOSSIBLE AND THAT IS LUCKY, not a scope cut that had to be policed: przez is verified NEW, so 'closed BY somebody' cannot be built with taught material at all. Named on slide 5 anyway, because a learner who knows the English passive will reach for it.

SINGULAR ONLY, inherited unchanged from b2_participle_pass and for its reason, not a fresh one: zrobione is the neuter singular here and nothing else, while it is also the non-virile plural and zrobieni the virile one — a form that means two things is what the AGENTS homograph rule says to keep out until it can be named. No plural appears on a slide, in a board, or as a distractor.

PISANIE IS ALL CLOZE, per the James-locked hard cap: every sentence in this unit is COMPOSED (noun + copula + participle built from parts), so none of them may be typed whole at any length. FIVE of the twelve blank the teaching point itself — the copula, which has exactly five distinct forms available here (jest, byl, byla, bylo, bedzie) and cannot supply a sixth without duplicating an answer within the stage. The remaining SEVEN blank the agreeing participle, logged per item under the queue's fallback clause; that is not a dodge, since the participle still agreeing under a changed tense is precisely the unit's second fact, and it is the half a learner drops. All twelve answers are distinct, checked with a mirror of the engine's norm().

NO FABRICATED NON-WORDS anywhere. Every quiz distractor is a real taught form doing the wrong job — a copula of the wrong gender or tense, or a participle that agrees correctly but means something else (zapłacony offered against ugotowany, zrobiona against ugotowana).

ADJECTIVE POVERTY AVOIDED RATHER THAN HIT: gotowy ('ready'), the obvious English gloss for several of these, is verified NEW and appears nowhere; the glosses stay on 'cooked', 'done', 'paid', 'written', 'open', 'closed'. NEGATION IS ABSENT by choice — nie + byl is legal and owned, but the unit is about tense and agreement, and adding a negated copula would put a third moving part in sentences that already have two.

intro.title: The sentence you built last unit has a name
intro.body:
Last unit you put a participle after jest and left it there:

Sklep jest zamknięty. — The shop is closed.

That sentence has a name. It is the passive. The noun at the front is not doing anything — it is what somebody else's work was done to. The shop did not close itself; someone closed it, and the sentence talks about the shop rather than about them.

English builds it the same way, out of the same two pieces: a form of to be, plus a participle. is closed · was written · will be paid.

So neither the idea nor the machinery is new to you. What is new is that Polish lets you move this construction through time, and that is the whole of this unit: jest, był, będzie.

intro.title: The past — and both words carry the gender
intro.body:
To move the passive into the past, change jest to the past of być. You have had these three since A2: był, była, było.

Sklep jest zamknięty. → Sklep był zamknięty.
Apteka jest zamknięta. → Apteka była zamknięta.
Biuro jest zamknięte. → Biuro było zamknięte.

Read down the endings rather than across. Both words agree with the noun, and they agree in the same direction every time: był … zamknięty, była … zamknięta, było … zamknięte.

This is the one thing in the unit that can go wrong. It is easy to change the tense and leave the participle behind — to reach for był and then say zamknięta after it. The noun decides both words, not one of them.
intro.body_pl: Czas przeszły: był / była / było + imiesłów. Oba wyrazy zgodne z rzeczownikiem.

intro.title: The future — where A2's gift comes back, and only half applies
intro.body:
The future uses będzie, and here something you were given at A2 returns.

When you learned the future of być, the headline was that będzie has no gender: the same word for a man, a woman and a table. That is still completely true.

But the participle after it has not changed its mind. It still agrees with the noun, exactly as it did in the past.

Sklep będzie zamknięty.
Apteka będzie zamknięta.
Biuro będzie zamknięte.

So the future is the odd one out in this construction. In the past, both words move. In the future, the first word stands still and the second one keeps moving.
intro.body_pl: Czas przyszły: będzie bez rodzaju, imiesłów z rodzajem.

intro.title: The same thing seen from the other side
intro.body:
Slides 2 and 3 held the tense still and moved the gender. Turn it around: hold the noun still and move the tense.

Obiad jest ugotowany. — The dinner is cooked.
Obiad był ugotowany. — The dinner was cooked.
Obiad będzie ugotowany. — The dinner will be cooked.

obiad is masculine in all three, so ugotowany never moves at all. Only the first word changes, and all it is doing is carrying the time.

That is the shape worth holding on to: one word for when, one word for what was done, and the noun in front deciding how the second one ends.
intro.body_pl: Rzeczownik bez zmian: rodzaj stały, czas ruchomy.

intro.title: What this unit does not cover
intro.body:
Three limits, named so you know where the edge is rather than walking into it.

First, and this is a real distinction rather than a scope note: what you have here describes a state — the result, how things stood. Sklep był zamknięty says the shop stood closed. Polish has a second passive for the action itself, the moment of the closing, and it is built with a different verb. That verb is not taught in this course yet, and it appears nowhere in this unit.

Second: you cannot yet say who did it. English adds by somebody; Polish has its own way of doing that and it needs a word you do not have. Every sentence here is about the thing, never about the person behind it.

Third: singular only, the same limit the last unit set and for the same reason. The plural of these participles is a shape that means two different things at once, and it has to be named properly before it is safe to use.

quiz.explain: sklep is masculine, so the past of być takes its masculine form — the same był you have used since A2, now carrying a participle after it.
The participle at the end already tells you the gender: zamknięta is feminine, so the word in front of it has to be była. Both words answer to apteka.
biuro is neuter, so było — and zamknięte agrees with it in the same direction.
The future needs no gender on this word at all. będzie would be the answer here whatever the noun was.
będzie gave you no clue, because it never does. The gender has to come off apteka, so the participle ends in -a. zamknięta is the right shape and the wrong meaning.
obiad is masculine and był has already agreed with it; the participle now does the same. zapłacony agrees correctly but would have the dinner paid rather than cooked.
zupa is feminine, so both words end in -a. zrobiona is feminine too and says the soup was made rather than cooked.
praca is feminine. This is the error the unit warns about: reaching for był after changing the tense, when zrobiona at the end is already telling you it must be była.
rachunek is masculine, so -y. napisany is masculine as well, but a bill is paid rather than written.
One word for the future, whatever the noun. The gender is still visible — but on napisany, not here.
okno is neuter, so było. The -e on otwarte and the -o on było are the same fact said twice.
zadanie is neuter, so -e. napisane is neuter too, but it would say the task was written out rather than done.
